requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2oct` has the signature `int2oct(in integer invalue, in integer length) return octetstring`.
requirements.original: int2oct(in integer invalue, in integer length) return octetstring

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `int2oct` converts a single integer value into a single octetstring value.
requirements.original: This function converts a single integer value to a single octetstring value.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: The octetstring returned by `int2oct` IS exactly `length` octets long.
requirements.original: The resulting string is length octets long.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: For the conversion performed by `int2oct`, an octetstring SHALL be interpreted as a positive base 16 integer value.
requirements.original: For the purposes of this conversion, an octetstring shall be interpreted as a positive base 16 integer value.

ambiguity.issue: The value 0 is a valid result/argument, so the octetstring is interpreted as a non-negative (not strictly positive) integer.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2oct`, the rightmost hexadecimal digit IS the least significant digit.
requirements.original: The rightmost hexadecimal digit is least significant, the leftmost hexadecimal digit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2oct`, the leftmost hexadecimal digit IS the most significant digit.
requirements.original: The rightmost hexadecimal digit is least significant, the leftmost hexadecimal digit is the most significant.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: The octetstring produced by `int2oct` SHALL contain a number of hexadecimal digits that is a multiple of 2, since one octet is composed of two hexadecimal digits.
requirements.original: The number of hexadecimal digits provided shall be multiples of 2 since one octet is composed of two hexadecimal digits.

readings: The result of `int2oct` SHALL contain an even number of hexadecimal digits (i.e. a leading zero digit is added when the value has an odd number of significant digits).
Some user-provided hexadecimal digit sequence SHALL have an even length.
ambiguity.issue: 'The number of hexadecimal digits provided' does not say who provides the digits; int2oct takes no hexadecimal input, so the first reading (property of the result) was chosen.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: In the conversion performed by `int2oct`, the hexadecimal digits 0 to F represent the decimal values 0 to 15 respectively.
requirements.original: The hexadecimal digits 0 to F represent the decimal values 0 to 15 respectively.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.condition: the conversion yields fewer digits than length octets
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields fewer hexadecimal digits than specified by the `length` parameter, `int2oct` SHALL pad the resulting octetstring on the left with zeros.
requirements.original: If the conversion yields a value with fewer hexadecimal digits than specified in the length parameter, then the hexstring shall be padded on the left with zeros.

readings: If the result has fewer than 2*length hexadecimal digits, `int2oct` SHALL pad the octetstring on the left with zero digits up to `length` octets.
If the result has fewer than `length` hexadecimal digits, `int2oct` SHALL pad it on the left with zeros up to `length` hexadecimal digits.
ambiguity.issue: The sentence was copied from int2hex: it says 'hexstring' instead of 'octetstring' and compares hexadecimal digits with 'length', which counts octets (C.1.6-s003). Reading 1 was chosen because it is consistent with C.1.6-s003.

requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `int2oct`.
requirements.original: In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.canonical: If `invalue` is less than zero, the call of `int2oct` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more octets than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.subject: ent:fn-int2oct
requirements.condition: the result needs more than length octets
requirements.canonical: If the conversion yields a return value with more octets than specified by `length`, the call of `int2oct` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.original: invalue is less than zero; the conversion yields a return value with more octets than specified by length. In addition to the general error causes in clause 16.1.2, error causes are:

requirements.canonical: The charstring returned by `int2str` IS always the decimal representation of the integer value.
requirements.original: This function converts the integer value into its string equivalent (the base of the return string is always decimal).

requirements.subject: ent:fn-char2int

requirements.original: char2int(in charstring invalue) return integer

requirements.canonical: The integer value returned by `char2int` IS the encoding (character code) of the character in `invalue`.
requirements.original: The integer value describes the 8-bit encoding of the character.

ambiguity.issue: The range 0..127 corresponds to a 7-bit character code; the text calls it an 8-bit encoding.

requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2oct` has the signature `char2oct(in charstring invalue) return octetstring`.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-char2oct
requirements.canonical: The predefined function `char2oct` converts a charstring `invalue` into an octetstring.
requirements.original: This function converts a charstring invalue to an octetstring.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-char2oct

requirements.original: Each octet of the octetstring will contain the Recommendation ITU-T T.50 [4] codes (according to the IRV) of the appropriate characters of invalue.

requirements.subject: ent:fn-char2oct
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of clause 16.1.2 SHALL apply to `char2oct`.
requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
